newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-SELECTOR CONCEDES DIFFICULTIES WITH TENDULKAR.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SELECTOR CONCEDES DIFFICULTIES WITH TENDULKAR.

text.p: India's chief selector Ramakant Desai conceded on Friday there were differences of opinion with captain Sachin Tendulkar over the team for next week's four-nation Asian Cup one-day tournament.
On Wednesday the Calcutta-based Bengali language daily Aajkal quoted Tendulkar as saying he had been given a sub-standard team.
"They have saddled me with a B-grade team," Tendulkar was quoted as saying. "I can't say I have been given the best team to lead."
Desai said there had been differences over some of the players in the squad but added: "Tendulkar has a wise head and knows the futility of crying over spilt milk in public."
An official from the Board of Control for Cricket in India, who did not want to be identified, said Tendulkar had not got the team he had wanted.

"Tendulkar was keen to have middle-order batsmen Vinod Kambli and wicketkeeper Nayan Mongia in the squad but instead the majority among the selectors picked (former captain) Mohammed Azharuddin and Saba Karim," he said.
